title: Descent of finitely presented modules and of maps between fixed models
statement: Let I be a directed set and let (S_i)_{i\in I} be an inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, where S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i) for Noetherian rings R_i, and let S=\varprojlim_i S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R). Fix i\in I, let X_i be a finitely presented S_i-scheme [def-pc-scheme], put X=X_i\times_{S_i}S and X_j=X_i\times_{S_i}S_j for j\ge i [def-pc-base-change]; for a module F_j on X_j and j'\ge j write (F_j)_{j'} and (F_j)_X for its pullbacks to X_{j'} and X. Then: (1) (modules) for every finitely presented quasi-coherent \mathcal{O}_X-module M [pqf-def-coherent] there are j\ge i, a finitely presented quasi-coherent \mathcal{O}_{X_j}-module M_j and an isomorphism (M_j)_X\cong M; (2) (morphisms) given j\ge i, finitely presented quasi-coherent \mathcal{O}_{X_j}-modules F_j,G_j and an \mathcal{O}_X-linear map \varphi:(F_j)_X\to(G_j)_X, there are j'\ge j and an \mathcal{O}_{X_{j'}}-linear map \varphi_{j'}:(F_j)_{j'}\to(G_j)_{j'} whose pullback to X is \varphi (through the canonical isomorphisms ((F_j)_{j'})_X\cong(F_j)_X, ((G_j)_{j'})_X\cong(G_j)_X).

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (finite-presentation descent of modules and morphisms)

proof.text: When X_i is affine, every X_j and X are affine as well: write X_i=Spec(B_i), X_j=Spec(B_j) with B_j=B_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j, and X=Spec(B) with B=B_i\otimes_{R_i}R; since R is the directed colimit of the R_j (S=Spec(R)=\varprojlim Spec(R_j)) and tensor product commutes with directed colimits, B is the directed colimit of the B_j. A finitely presented quasi-coherent module on an affine scheme is the sheaf associated to a finitely presented module, maps of quasi-coherent modules are maps of the modules, and pullback is extension of scalars. Thus the module, map, and equality assertions are exactly the affine ring statement [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine]. The Noetherian hypothesis on the R_i is not used anywhere in this proof.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR, first proof (affine case)

proof.text: For general X_i, which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because it is finitely presented over the quasi-compact, quasi-separated S_i, choose a finite affine open cover (U_a)_a of X_i; its base changes cover X_j and X, and each (U_a)_j, (U_a)_X is affine. Since X_i is quasi-separated, every pairwise intersection U_a\cap U_b, every triple intersection U_a\cap U_b\cap U_c, and every intersection of two affine opens of X_i is quasi-compact; cover each of the finitely many such opens that occur below by finitely many affine opens of X_i. Agreement of two maps of quasi-coherent modules, and the cocycle condition, are local, so they hold on such an open as soon as they hold on each member of its finite affine cover. Module descent: apply the object clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] on each U_a to get models M_a. On each affine V_{ab,c} of the cover of U_a\cap U_b apply the map clause to the given identification of the pullbacks of M_a and M_b and to its inverse, and the equality clause to the two composites with the identities, so it descends to an isomorphism \theta_{ab,c}; apply the equality clause on the affines covering each V_{ab,c}\cap V_{ab,c'} so that the \theta_{ab,c} agree there and glue to an isomorphism \theta_{ab} on (U_a\cap U_b)_j; apply the equality clause on the affines covering each triple intersection so that the cocycle condition \theta_{ac}=\theta_{bc}\circ\theta_{ab} holds. Map descent: apply the map clause on each U_a and the equality clause on the affines covering each U_a\cap U_b so the local maps agree on overlaps. All of this is finitely many applications, each holding from some stage on and preserved by further pullback; since I is directed, one common later stage j works. The descended modules and the isomorphisms \theta_{ab} then glue (Zariski gluing of quasi-coherent sheaves) to a finitely presented quasi-coherent module on X_j, and the descended local maps glue to a map; pulling back the glued data gives the original module or map, since this holds on each (U_a)_X compatibly with the gluing data.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR, first proof (general case: Zariski gluing from the affine case)

proof.text: For clause (1), run the finite-cover construction on the given module M and retain the descended local modules and comparison isomorphisms; their glued module M_j is finitely presented and its pullback is M. For clause (2), run it simultaneously on F_j, G_j, and the given map, so the descended local maps glue to a map phi_{j'}:(F_j)_{j'}\to(G_j)_{j'} whose pullback is phi. The identifications ((F_j)_{j'})_X\cong(F_j)_X and ((G_j)_{j'})_X\cong(G_j)_X are the canonical associativity identifications for iterated base change.

The affine case is isolated as the strictly narrower ring-level finite-presentation colimit statement; the general case applies that result on finite affine covers and quasi-compact overlaps, descends the finite compatibility data at one common stage, and glues by the Zariski construction. No sorry-free project declaration states the item.
